knowledge:
- key_parameters: domains.mat=A BED-like data frame where the second and third columns are genomic coordinates of domain anchor midpoints, used in extractBoundaries() ;; featureType=The type of feature space to construct (e.g., "distance" for log2 distance to nearest peak, "overlap", "count", "percent") in createTADdata() ;; resampling=The resampling strategy to balance boundary vs non-boundary classes (e.g., "rus" for random under-sampling) in createTADdata() ;; threshold=The probability threshold (t) used to filter bases before clustering in preciseTAD() ;; DBSCAN_params=A list containing eps (epsilon neighborhood distance) and MinPts (minimum number of points) for DBSCAN clustering in preciseTAD() ;; BaseProbs=Logical indicating whether to return base-level probabilities in preciseTAD(); can cause memory issues if set to TRUE for large regions
- alternatives: Arrowhead (part of Juicebox) and Peakachu are mentioned as tools to call TAD boundaries from Hi-C data. preciseTAD is preferred when high-resolution Hi-C data is unavailable or costly, as it predicts base-level boundaries using genomic annotations. Support Vector Machines (SVM) via e1071::svm can also be used on the created data matrix, but Random Forest is the default and showed better performance.
- when_to_use: Use when you want to identify TAD or loop boundaries at base-level resolution, especially when high-resolution Hi-C data is unavailable but high-resolution functional genomic annotations (like CTCF, RAD21, SMC3, ZNF143 ChIP-seq data) are available.
- pitfalls: Setting BaseProbs = TRUE in preciseTAD() can result in a very large vector of base-specific probabilities, potentially causing memory issues for large genomic regions. Pre-trained models were trained on cancer cell lines (GM12878 and K562), so caution should be exercised when applying them to normal cell lines. Ensure the resolution parameter matches the resolution of the Hi-C data used to call the ground-truth boundaries.

workflows.name: model_training_and_prediction
workflows.intent: Build a random forest model from ground-truth TAD boundaries and genomic annotations, and use it to predict base-level boundary regions and points.
input: arrowhead_gm12878_5kb (BED-like data frame of TAD coordinates)
tfbsList (GRangesList of transcription factor binding sites or path to BED files)
workflows.stages: 1. Extract unique boundaries using extractBoundaries() ;; 2. Convert BED files to GRangesList using bedToGRangesList() ;; 3. Create training and testing data using createTADdata() ;; 4. Perform recursive feature elimination using TADrfe() ;; 5. Train a random forest model using TADrandomForest() ;; 6. Predict precise boundaries at base-level resolution using preciseTAD() ;; 7. Format predicted boundaries for Juicebox using juicer_func()
workflows.code:
bounds <- extractBoundaries(domains.mat = arrowhead_gm12878_5kb, filter = FALSE, CHR = c("CHR1", "CHR22"), resolution = 5000)
data("tfbsList")
set.seed(123)
tadData <- createTADdata(bounds.GR = bounds, resolution = 5000, genomicElements.GR = tfbsList, featureType = "distance", resampling = "rus", trainCHR = "CHR1", predictCHR = "CHR22")
set.seed(123)
rfe_res <- TADrfe(trainData = tadData[[1]], tuneParams = list(ntree = 500, nodesize = 1), cvFolds = 5, cvMetric = "Accuracy", verbose = TRUE)
tfbsList_filt <- tfbsList[names(tfbsList) %in% c("Gm12878-Ctcf-Broad", "Gm12878-Rad21-Haib", "Gm12878-Smc3-Sydh", "Gm12878-Znf143-Sydh")]
set.seed(123)
tadData <- createTADdata(bounds.GR = bounds, resolution = 5000, genomicElements.GR = tfbsList_filt, featureType = "distance", resampling = "rus", trainCHR = "CHR1", predictCHR = "CHR22")
set.seed(123)
tadModel <- TADrandomForest(trainData = tadData[[1]], testData = tadData[[2]], tuneParams = list(mtry = 2, ntree = 500, nodesize = 1), cvFolds = 3, cvMetric = "Accuracy", verbose = FALSE, model = TRUE, importances = TRUE, impMeasure = "MDA", performances = TRUE)
set.seed(123)
pt <- preciseTAD(genomicElements.GR = tfbsList_filt, featureType = "distance", CHR = "CHR22", chromCoords = list(17000000, 18000000), tadModel = tadModel[[1]], threshold = 1, verbose = TRUE, parallel = NULL, DBSCAN_params = list(eps = c(30000), MinPts = c(100)), slope = 5000, genome = "hg19", BaseProbs = TRUE)
pt_juice <- juicer_func(pt$PTBP)

workflows.name: cross_cell_type_prediction
workflows.intent: Predict precise TAD boundaries in a new cell type using a pre-trained model and cell-type-specific genomic annotations.
input: ctcf.bed, rad21.bed, smc3.bed, znf143.bed (BED files of transcription factor binding sites for the target cell type)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the pre-trained model using readRDS() ;; 2. Read and convert target cell-type BED files into a GRangesList using bedToGRangesList() ;; 3. Predict precise boundaries using preciseTAD()
workflows.code:
tadModel <- readRDS("~/Downloads/CHR22_GM12878_5kb_Peakachu.rds")
ctcf <- as.data.frame(read.delim("http://raw.githubusercontent.com/stilianoudakis/preciseTAD_supplementary/master/data/bed/hela/ctcf.bed", sep = "\t", header = FALSE))
rad21 <- as.data.frame(read.delim("http://raw.githubusercontent.com/stilianoudakis/preciseTAD_supplementary/master/data/bed/hela/rad21.bed", sep = "\t", header = FALSE))
smc3 <- as.data.frame(read.delim("http://raw.githubusercontent.com/stilianoudakis/preciseTAD_supplementary/master/data/bed/hela/smc3.bed", sep = "\t", header = FALSE))
znf143 <- as.data.frame(read.delim("http://raw.githubusercontent.com/stilianoudakis/preciseTAD_supplementary/master/data/bed/hela/znf143.bed", sep = "\t", header = FALSE))
helaList <- list(ctcf, rad21, smc3, znf143)
hela.GR <- bedToGRangesList(bedList=helaList, bedNames=c("Ctcf", "Rad21", "Smc3", "Znf143"), signal=5)
set.seed(123)
pt <- preciseTAD(genomicElements.GR = hela.GR, featureType = "distance", CHR = "CHR22", chromCoords = list(25500000, 27500000), tadModel = tadModel[[1]], threshold = 1.0, verbose = FALSE, parallel = NULL, DBSCAN_params = list(30000, 100), slope = 5000, BaseProbs = FALSE, savetobed = FALSE)
